status.note: Chosen for modality. Tooltip established that layering has no home; a dialog adds focus containment, background inertness and a dismissal key, and none of those are the same problem. Sourced from the W3C ARIA APG modal dialog pattern. SPIKE 2026-09-02: rebound onto the native `<dialog>` element, which supplies containment, inertness, focus restoration and Escape from the platform rather than from a declaration. See the binding's notes for what that measured.

intent.purpose: Interrupts what a person was doing to ask for something that cannot wait, and refuses to let them continue until they answer or leave.
behaviour: Shows over the page with everything behind it made inert: not merely covered, but unreachable by pointer, by Tab and by a screen reader's virtual cursor.
Moves focus inside when it opens, onto the first meaningful control rather than the close button, and holds focus inside for as long as it is open.
Returns focus, on close, to whatever had it before — otherwise a keyboard user is dropped at the top of the document.
Closes on Escape from anywhere inside it.
Names itself from its own title, so it is announced as the thing it is asking about rather than as an unnamed dialog.
notFor: Anything that can be said in place. A dialog stops everything; a message that could have been a line of text under a field should be.
Non-modal side content. A panel that lets you keep working is a drawer or a popover, and modality is the whole difference.
Nesting. A dialog opened from a dialog leaves a person two escapes from where they were, and no design here covers where focus returns.
Anything long enough to scroll on a phone. A full-screen sheet is a different pattern with different dismissal rules.

open.description: The dialog is showing and holding focus.
open.visual: The scrim covers the page and the panel appears above it.

size.description: How wide the panel is. A contiguous subset of the canon's ladder.

a11y.keyboard: Escape closes from anywhere inside, supplied by the platform. Tab and Shift+Tab cycle within the dialog and cannot reach the page behind it.
notes: Focus containment, background inertness, focus restoration and Escape are all supplied by the PLATFORM, because the binding renders a native `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()`. None of the four is expressible in this contract and none had to be: they follow from an element name.

The containment is not a trap, and that is deliberate on the W3C's part rather than a shortfall. Tab cannot reach the page behind, but it can reach the browser's own chrome before cycling back. The APG's wording — that Tab does not move focus outside the dialog — describes a hand-rolled implementation; the platform's behaviour is what the W3C's own accessibility group settled on.

The dialog is named by its title. A dialog with no title is announced as an unnamed dialog, and NOTHING DETECTS THAT — not even axe, whose rule for it matches `[role="dialog"]` literally and so skips a native `<dialog>` entirely. The title slot is `required` here, which is the only thing standing between a consumer and a silently unnamed dialog.

There is no Escape key on a phone. A modal with no visible close control is unclosable on iOS, where the platform supplies no backstop, so an `actions` slot that always contains a way out is a consumer obligation this contract cannot check.

Pressing the backdrop closes it, declared by `dismisses`. The mechanism is worth knowing because it is not what it looks like: the backdrop is a pseudo-element and is never an event target, so a press on it reports THE DIALOG ITSELF as the target. `outside-press` therefore means a press on the region rather than on any descendant, and a press inside the panel correctly does nothing.

title.description: What the dialog is asking about. Required: it is the dialog's accessible name.

actions.description: The buttons that resolve it. Fills the `actions` part.

root.description: The dialog itself. Named by its title, and the region focus is held inside. It is ONE node, not a scrim wrapping a panel: the platform paints the layer behind it and does not give that layer an element.

title.description: The heading. Supplies the dialog's accessible name.

actions.description: The row of buttons that resolve it.
